subject: two or more spatial fields in INLA

messages.author: ade2a2fcffad1aa8
messages.subject: two or more spatial fields in INLA
parts:
Dear INLA-helpers

i was wondering if INLA can handle more than one spatial field, for example two fields with different meshes (or two spde-models):
y = A1*z1 + A2*z2 + e
z1 ~ N(0,Q1)
z2 ~ N(0,Q2)
e ~ N(0,sigma*I)

It would be great if you could help look at the following test codes for the above model..
Thank you very much for your help!

Ran.

## Test codes:

n = 100
loc1 = matrix(runif(n*2),n,2)

mesh1 =
  inla.mesh.create.helper(points=loc1,
                          cutoff=0.1,
                          max.edge=c(0.2,1),
                          min.angle=c(30,30),
                          offset=c(0.1,0.3))

loc2 = matrix(runif(n*2),n,2)

mesh2 =
  inla.mesh.create.helper(points=loc2,
                          cutoff=0.1,
                          max.edge=c(10,100),
                          min.angle=c(26,21),
                          offset=c(1,10))

#### Calculate mapping between the mesh nodes and the observation locations:
#  A: mapping stations to mesh nodes
A1 = inla.spde.make.A(mesh1, loc=loc1)
A2 = inla.spde.make.A(mesh2, loc=loc2)


#### Create SPDE objects
spde1 = inla.spde2.matern(mesh1, alpha=2)
summary(spde1)

spde2  = inla.spde2.matern(mesh2, alpha=2)
summary(spde2)

#### Simulate "the true" fields
true.kappa = sqrt(8)/0.3 ## Spatial range 0.3
true.tau   = 1/sqrt(4*pi*true.kappa^2) ## Variance = 1
true.field1 = inla.spde.sample(spde1, theta=log(c(true.tau, true.kappa)))
true.field2 = inla.spde.sample(spde2, theta=log(c(true.tau, true.kappa)))

y = as.vector(A1 %*% true.field1) + as.vector(A2 %*% true.field2) + rnorm(n, sd=0.1)

#### Writing INLA formulas and Calculating results
y = as.vector(y)

data.stack = inla.stack(data=list(y=y),
                        A = list(A1,A2),
                        effects=list(list(field1=1:mesh1$n),
                                         list(field2=1:mesh2$n)))

data  = list(y=y, field1 = 1:mesh1$n, field2 = 1:mesh2$n)
formula = y ~ -1 + f(field1, model = spde1) + f(field2, model = spde2)

# This gives an error back:
result =
  inla(formula,
       data = inla.stack.data(data.stack, spde1=spde1, spde2 = spde2),
       family = "normal",
       control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(data.stack)), verbose=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] two or more spatial fields in INLA
parts:
Hi Ran,
This works for me.

Try running inla.update(testing=TRUE). (There was an error for these
types of models, but it was fixed a while ago). If there is still a
problem, please tell me the version of R you're running, the operating
system, and exactly what the error message is.

Thanks

Dan
